summary: aiosendletter exfiltrates %LOCALAPPDATA%\logs to hardcoded Cloudflare Worker after UAC elevation
details: The package ships a module (e.py) that prompts for administrator elevation via UAC, archives the contents of %LOCALAPPDATA%\logs with shutil.make_archive, and POSTs the resulting zip to a hardcoded attacker-controlled endpoint at https://sparkling-pine-f202.stilluer-sweden.workers.dev/ using requests.post. The %LOCALAPPDATA%\logs tree commonly contains Discord, browser, and game-tool artifacts including session data. The package's PyPI summary ("Safe bug reporter for sending local logs via Cloudflare Workers") and identifiers such as aiosendletter_logs are cover-story framing for bulk exfiltration of installer-owned data. Separately, pyproject.toml declares the Python stdlib name "ctypes" as an unpinned PyPI runtime dependency, causing pip to resolve and install whatever package currently occupies that registry name and execute its lifecycle code on the installer's machine — a dependency-confusion install-time code path in addition to the primary stealer payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
